function.name: aggregate_data
function.description: Group aggregation operations on data: group stats, sum, mean, count, distinct count, variance, stddev, median, p25/p75/p90/p95/arbitrary percentile, etc. Supported operations: sum, mean/avg, min, max, count, count_distinct/n_unique, variance/var, stddev/std, median, p25/p75/p90/p95, percentile:N/pct:N, first, last. Example: aggregate_data(file_path='sales.csv', group_by='region', aggregations='sales:sum,profit:mean,users:count_distinct,revenue:p95')

file_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

group_by.description: Group-by column name (optional, comma-separated for multiple)

aggregations.description: Aggregation operations, format: 'column:op', comma-separated for multiple. Ops: sum, mean/avg, min, max, count, count_distinct, variance, stddev, median, p90, p95, percentile:N, etc.

function.name: apply_patch
function.description: Apply one transactional patch across files. The patch must start with '*** Begin Patch' and end with '*** End Patch'. Use '*** Add File: path', '*** Update File: path', '*** Delete File: path', optional '*** Move to: path', and @@ context hunks. Added lines start with +; removed lines with -; unchanged context lines with a space.

dry_run.description: Validate and return the diff without changing files

function.name: arxiv_search
function.description: Search arxiv for academic papers. Returns title, authors, abstract, arxiv ID, PDF URL, categories, and publication date. Supports category filtering (e.g. 'cs.AI', 'cs.LG', 'math.CO') and sorting. Max 100 results per query. Example: arxiv_search(query='transformer attention mechanism', max_results=20, category='cs.CL')

query.description: Search query (keywords, title, author name, etc.)

category.description: ArXiv category filter (optional). Common: cs.AI, cs.LG, cs.CL, cs.CV, math.CO, stat.ML, physics

function.name: bibtex_generate
function.description: Generate BibTeX entries from paper metadata. Accepts paper objects from arxiv_search or semantic_scholar_search results. Outputs standard .bib format. Example: bibtex_generate(papers=[{title: 'Attention Is All You Need', authors: ['Vaswani et al.'], year: 2017, arxiv_id: '1706.03762'}])

papers.description: Array of paper objects. Each should have: title, authors (array), year, and optionally arxiv_id, doi, url, venue

output_file.description: Optional file path to write the .bib file. If not provided, returns the BibTeX content as text.

function.name: bin_data
function.description: Bin numeric columns (equal-width / equal-frequency), counting records per bin and summarizing metrics. Suitable for analyzing data distribution and generating histogram data.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

function.name: clinical_trials_search
function.description: Search ClinicalTrials.gov for clinical trials. Returns NCT ID, title, status, phase, conditions, interventions, and primary outcome measures. No API key required. Example: clinical_trials_search(query='CRISPR cancer immunotherapy', max_results=10, status='RECRUITING')

query.description: Search query (condition, intervention, NCT ID, etc.)

status.description: Filter by study status (optional): RECRUITING, COMPLETED, ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, NOT_YET_RECRUITING, TERMINATED, SUSPENDED, WITHDRAWN

phase.description: Filter by phase (optional): EARLY_PHASE1, PHASE1, PHASE2, PHASE3, PHASE4, NA

function.name: code_search
function.description: Find code definitions by symbol name and kind; use grep for exact text lookup.

query.description: Symbol name, regex, or * wildcard pattern

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from page.next_cursor; reuse only with identical parameters

function.name: consistency_check
function.description: Check data consistency: type mismatches in string columns, out-of-range values in numeric columns, and cross-column validation. Custom rules can be provided as JSON.

data_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

function.name: contribution_data
function.description: Calculate contribution ratio (percentage) and cumulative ratio (Pareto analysis / 80-20 rule) of each dimension value to the metric column. Outputs dimension value, metric value, ratio (%), cumulative (%). Dimension values beyond top_n are merged into 'Other'. Suitable for questions like 'sales ratio by region', 'which categories contribute 80% of revenue? (Pareto analysis)'. Example: contribution_data(file_path='sales.csv', dimension_column='category', metric_column='revenue', top_n=15)

file_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

dimension_column.description: Dimension column name (column used for grouping)

metric_column.description: Metric column name (column used for sum calculation)

top_n.description: Show top N dimension values (default 20, rest grouped as "Other")

function.name: correlate_data
function.description: Compute correlation matrix between numeric columns. Returns Pearson correlation coefficients between -1 and 1.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

columns.description: Comma-separated list of numeric columns to correlate (default: all numeric columns)

function.name: data_stats
function.description: Compute detailed per-column statistics (no grouping): count, nulls and null rate, distinct count and distinct rate, mean, stddev, variance, min, max, median, p25/p75/p90/p95 percentiles; for string columns also shows shortest/longest/average length and most frequent value. Difference from aggregate_data: data_stats is per-column overall stats (no grouping), aggregate_data is grouped aggregation. Example: data_stats(file_path='data.csv', columns='age,income,region')

file_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

columns.description: Column names to compute statistics for, comma-separated (optional, defaults to all numeric columns)

function.name: describe_table
function.description: View the structure of a specified table (column names, types, nullable). Supports SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL.

function.name: diff
function.description: Compare two files or a file against a string, returning a unified diff. Use path_a + path_b to compare two files, or path_a + content_b to compare a file against given content.

path_b.description: Second file path (the 'after' side). Either path_b or content_b is required.

content_b.description: Alternative to path_b: compare path_a against this string content.

context.description: Number of context lines around changes (default: 3)

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous page

function.name: enter_worktree
function.description: Create a new git worktree for isolated parallel work. Use this when a subagent needs to work on a separate branch without conflicting with other agents or the main working tree. NOTE: this only creates the worktree on disk — it does NOT switch the agent's runtime working directory. To run subsequent tools inside the new worktree, the host must bind it as the session working_dir (e.g. via the /worktree command), not via this tool.

branch.description: Branch name for the new worktree (created if it does not exist)

base.description: Base branch or commit to create from (defaults to HEAD)

path_suffix.description: Optional custom directory name under .worktrees/ (defaults to sanitized branch name)

repo_path.description: Repository path (defaults to current working directory)

function.name: excel_info
function.description: Get basic info about an Excel file: sheet list, row/column counts, etc.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the Excel file

function.name: excel_load
function.description:
Load Excel sheet(s) into Polars DataFrame(s) and save as Parquet/CSV. This bridges Excel data into the data processing pipeline — after loading, use filter_data, aggregate_data, data_stats, transform_data, etc.

Supports:
- Single sheet: sheet='Sheet1' or sheet='0'
- Multiple sheets: sheets='Sheet1,Sheet2' or sheets='0,1,2'
- All sheets: sheets='all'
- Custom header row: header_row=2 means row index 2 (0-based) is the header (default 0)
- Skip rows: skip_rows=2 to ignore the first 2 rows entirely

file_path.description: Absolute path to the Excel file

sheet.description: Single worksheet name or index (e.g. 'Sheet1' or '0'). Use 'sheets' for multiple.

sheets.description: Multiple worksheets: comma-separated names/indices (e.g. 'Sheet1,Sheet2') or 'all' for all sheets. Overrides 'sheet'.

output_file.description: Output file path (default: same name with .parquet extension). For multiple sheets, a suffix is added.

header_row.description: 0-based row index of the header row (default 0). Use 1 if row 2 is the actual header, 2 if row 3, etc. Rows before the header are skipped.

max_rows.description: Maximum rows to load per sheet (default: all)

function.name: excel_profile
function.description: Profile an Excel file: detect column types, count nulls, compute basic statistics (min/max/mean for numbers). Useful for quick data quality assessment.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the Excel file

sheet.description: Worksheet name or index (e.g. 'Sheet1' or '0', defaults to first sheet)

max_rows.description: Maximum rows to profile (default: all rows)

function.name: excel_to_csv
function.description: Export an Excel worksheet to a CSV file.

sheet.description: Worksheet name or index (e.g. 'Sheet1' or '0', defaults to first sheet)

function.name: exit_worktree
function.description: Remove a clean managed git worktree while preserving its branch. Optionally merge the worktree branch into a target branch before removal.

worktree_path.description: Path to the worktree directory to remove

merge_to.description: If set, merge the worktree branch into this target branch before removal

repo_path.description: Repository path (defaults to current working directory)

function.name: exploratory_statistics
function.description: Compute exploratory descriptive statistics for numeric columns: valid/missing counts, mean, sample standard deviation, min, quartiles, max, skewness, and excess kurtosis. This tool never returns p-values, confidence intervals, or significance conclusions. For formal inference, write a reviewable Python/R script using SciPy, statsmodels, or established R packages and execute it with run_code.

columns.description: Column names to analyze, comma-separated (default: all numeric columns)

data_path.description: Absolute path to the data file (CSV, JSON, or Parquet)

function.name: export_data
function.description: Export processed data to CSV, JSON, or Parquet file.

function.name: export_text
function.description: Export processed text to a new file.

function.name: extract_pdf
function.description: Extract text content from PDF documents. Supports extracting all text, specified page ranges, or retrieving document metadata.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the PDF file

pages.description: Page range to extract (optional), e.g. '1-5', '1,3,7', or 'all' (default)

extract_metadata.description: Whether to also extract document metadata (default false)

function.name: filter_data
function.description: Filter a data file, supporting conditional expressions (comparisons, AND/OR combinations, contains matching, etc.). Returns a preview of the filtered data.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

filter.description: Filter condition. Supports: 'col > 100', 'col == "value"', 'col contains "text"', 'A > 10 AND B < 5', 'col starts_with "prefix"'

function.name: final_answer
function.description: Call this tool to return the final answer when you have gathered enough information to respond to the user

function.name: generate_chart
function.description: Generate data visualization charts (vega-lite v5 JSON spec). Supports line, bar, pie, scatter, area, heatmap, boxplot.

x_field.description: X axis field name (used as color grouping in pie charts)

y_field.description: Y axis field name (used as value in pie charts)

data.description: Chart data (array of JSON objects, each object's key maps to a field name)

output_format.description: Output format: 'json' (default, Vega-Lite spec) or 'html' (standalone HTML page with embedded chart)

function.name: git_blame
function.description: View line-by-line annotations for a file, showing the last author and commit for each line

file_path.description: File path to inspect (relative to repo root)

repo_path.description: Repository path (defaults to current working directory)

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from page.next_cursor; reuse only with identical parameters

function.name: git_branch
function.description: View, create, or switch Git branches. No args lists all branches; with name creates a new branch

repo_path.description: Repository path (defaults to current working directory)

name.description: New branch name (creates a branch if provided)

delete.description: Delete the specified branch (must be merged)

function.name: git_commit
function.description: Create a Git commit. Files must be staged via git add first. Only call this tool when explicitly requested by the user.

repo_path.description: Repository path (defaults to current working directory)

files.description: List of files to stage and commit (empty = commit all staged)

function.name: git_diff
function.description: View code diffs: unstaged changes, staged changes, or diffs between specified branches/commits

repo_path.description: Repository path (defaults to current working directory)

staged.description: Whether to view staged changes (default false)

target.description: Comparison target: branch name, commit hash, or HEAD~1

file_path.description: Show diff for specified file only

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from page.next_cursor; reuse only with identical parameters

function.name: git_log
function.description: View Git commit history, with options for count limit and format

repo_path.description: Repository path (defaults to current working directory)

function.name: git_status
function.description: View working directory status of the current repo: modified, staged, untracked files

repo_path.description: Repository path (defaults to current working directory)

function.name: glob
function.description: Find files by name pattern. Returns file paths matching a glob pattern (e.g. '**/*.rs', 'src/**/*.ts', '*.md'). Supports ** for recursive directory matching.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file names (e.g. '**/*.rs', 'src/**/*.ts', '*.md')

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous page

function.name: grep
function.description: Exact text search over file contents using a regex. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers; use code_search for symbol-oriented code discovery.

pattern.description: Regular expression pattern to search for

path.description: Directory or file path to search in (default: current directory)

context.description: Number of context lines before and after each match (default: 0)

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous page

function.name: image_fetch
function.description: Downloads an image from a URL and converts it to base64 encoding, suitable for LLM multimodal input. Parameters: url - image URL (required), max_size_mb - maximum file size in MB (optional, default 10MB)

function.name: join_data
function.description: Join two data files on common key columns. Supports inner, left, and outer joins. Useful for combining orders with customers, facts with dimensions, etc. Example: join_data(left_file='orders.csv', right_file='customers.csv', join_keys=['customer_id'], join_type='left')

left_file.description: Absolute path to the left (primary) data file

right_file.description: Absolute path to the right (lookup) data file

join_keys.description: Column names to join on (must exist in both files). At least 1 key required.

left_suffix.description: Suffix for duplicate column names from left file (default: '_left')

right_suffix.description: Suffix for duplicate column names from right file (default: '_right')

format.description: File format override for both files: 'csv', 'json', or 'parquet'

function.name: list_dir
function.description: List all files and subdirectories in a directory, returning a name list

path.description: Directory path to list, defaults to current directory

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous page

function.name: list_tables
function.description: List all tables in the database. Supports SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL.

function.name: list_worktrees
function.description: List all git worktrees in the repository, showing their paths and branches.

repo_path.description: Repository path (defaults to current working directory)

function.name: missing_value_analysis
function.description: Analyze missing values in a dataset: counts per column, percentage, pattern classification (all_missing, random_missing, monotonic), and imputation suggestions based on column type and missing rate.

data_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

function.name: multi_read_data
function.description: Read and concatenate multiple same-schema data files into a single DataFrame. Supports CSV, JSON, and Parquet. Maximum 50 files. Useful for merging monthly reports, log files, or sharded data. Example: multi_read_data(file_paths=['data/jan.csv','data/feb.csv','data/mar.csv'])

file_paths.description: List of absolute file paths to read (max 50). All files must have the same column schema.

format.description: File format: 'csv', 'json', or 'parquet' (optional, auto-detected per file)

preview_rows.description: Number of preview rows from the merged result (default 10)

function.name: outlier_detection
function.description: Detect outliers in numeric columns using IQR method (values beyond Q1 - k*IQR or Q3 + k*IQR) or Z-score method (values with |z| > threshold). Default threshold: 1.5 for IQR, 3.0 for Z-score.

data_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

columns.description: Column names to check, comma-separated (default: all numeric columns)

function.name: pdf_fetch
function.description: Download a PDF from a URL and extract its text content. Supports arxiv PDF links, direct URLs, and redirects. Useful for reading academic papers. Example: pdf_fetch(url='https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762', pages='1-10')

url.description: URL of the PDF to download (e.g. https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762)

pages.description: Page range to extract (optional). Examples: '1-5', '1,3,7', 'all'. Default: first 20 pages

function.name: pdf_info
function.description: Get basic information about a PDF document: page count, title, author, creation time, and other metadata. Does not extract text content.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the PDF file

function.name: pivot_data
function.description: Create pivot tables. Reshape data by grouping rows by one or more columns and pivoting another column's values into new columns.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

index.description: Column(s) to use as row index (comma-separated)

columns.description: Column whose unique values will become new columns

function.name: process_text
function.description: Process text: extract, merge, deduplicate lines, etc.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the text file

operation.description: Operation type: 'unique' (deduplicate), 'sort' (sort), 'reverse' (reverse lines), 'trim' (remove blank lines), 'head' (first N lines), 'tail' (last N lines)

count.description: Number of lines for head/tail operations

function.name: profile_data
function.description: [Quick data understanding - preferred tool] Automatically identifies each column as dimension or metric: computes missing rate, distinct rate, [min,max,mean,sum] for numeric columns, length range for string columns, and top 5 sample values. Output also includes column classification summary (dimension/metric/time column counts) and suggests follow-up analysis tools (topn_data, contribution_data, bin_data, etc.). Does not return detailed data, only a profile scan. Example: profile_data(file_path='sales.csv')

file_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

function.name: pubmed_search
function.description: Search PubMed (NCBI) for biomedical literature. Returns PMID, title, authors, abstract, journal, year, DOI, and MeSH terms. Supports date range filtering and sorting. Example: pubmed_search(query='CRISPR gene therapy cancer', max_results=20, sort='pub_date')

query.description: Search query (keywords, MeSH terms, author names, etc.)

function.name: rag_chunk_document
function.description: Preview document chunking results (does not build an index). Use to inspect chunking strategy and tune parameters.

function.name: ratio_data
function.description: Compute arithmetic expressions and ratios between columns. Supports +, -, *, / and parentheses, with optional grouping dimensions for within-group ratios. Suitable for computing profit margin, conversion rate, YoY/MoM, proportions, etc. Example: ratio_data(file_path='sales.csv', expressions='profit_margin:(revenue-cost)/revenue*100, ratio:cost/revenue')

file_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

expressions.description: Expression definitions, comma-separated. Format: 'alias:expression'. Expressions support +, -, *, / and parentheses, referencing column names and numeric constants. Example: 'margin:(revenue-cost)/revenue*100, ratio:a/b'

dimension_columns.description: Grouping dimension column names (optional, comma-separated). When specified, expressions are computed within each group

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read the complete spilled output of a previous tool call in bounded UTF-8 pages. Use the returned next_cursor until complete.

path.description: Exact artifact path returned by a previous tool result

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor returned by the previous read_artifact page

max_tokens.description: Maximum content tokens for this page (default and hard maximum: 3500)

expected_sha256.description: Optional full SHA-256 from the spill notice; fully verified on the first and final pages and bound into every cursor

function.name: read_data
function.description: Read data files (CSV, JSON, Parquet), returning basic info and a preview of the first rows.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

function.name: read_excel
function.description: Read Excel file (.xlsx/.xls/.xlsb/.ods), return sheet list and data preview.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the Excel file

sheet.description: Worksheet name or index (e.g. 'Sheet1' or '0', defaults to first sheet)

skip_rows.description: Number of rows to skip from the top (default 0). Use this when the file has title/metadata rows before the actual header row.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read compact line-numbered text with bounded output. Use offset/limit to paginate; prefer grep for known text.

path.description: Relative or absolute file path

function.name: read_word
function.description: Read Word document (.docx), extract text content.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the Word document

include_formatting.description: Whether to include formatting info (default false)

function.name: repo_map
function.description: Generate a codebase tree or AST-aware symbol map. Rust, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, and Java use Tree-sitter; unsupported syntax falls back to conservative text extraction.

path.description: Root directory to map (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum tree or symbol lines per page (default: 100)

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from page.next_cursor; reuse only with identical parameters

function.name: run_code
function.description: Execute Python/R/JavaScript/etc. code in the task working directory. For real analysis, save the script first and run it via `script_path` (a reviewed file); for quick exploration use `code`. Provide exactly one of the two. Returns stdout/stderr/exit code.

code.description: Inline code snippet for quick execution; mutually exclusive with `script_path`.

script_path.description: Relative path of a saved, reviewed script inside `working_dir`; mutually exclusive with `code`.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search content in text files, supports regular expressions.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the text file

context.description: Number of context lines before and after matches (default 0)

function.name: semantic_scholar_search
function.description: Search Semantic Scholar for academic papers. Returns rich metadata including citation count, references, fields of study. No API key required (rate-limited). Supports keyword search and paper ID lookup. Example: semantic_scholar_search(query='large language models', limit=20)

query.description: Search query (keywords, title, author)

fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return (optional). Default includes title, abstract, authors, citationCount, year, url, fieldsOfStudy, venue

year_range.description: Year range filter (optional). Format: '2020-2025' or '2020-' or '-2023'

fields_of_study.description: Filter by field of study (optional). E.g. 'Computer Science', 'Mathematics'

function.name: shell
function.description: Execute restricted shell commands (only safe read-only operations and code-related commands are allowed). Parameter: command - the command to execute. Note: only simple commands (program + args) are supported; pipes, redirects, command substitution, and other shell syntax are not allowed.

command.description: The command to execute (only safe commands in the whitelist; shell syntax like pipes/redirects/command substitution is not supported)

timeout.description: Command timeout in seconds (foreground default: 60, max: 300; background uses the cell runtime limit)

background.description: Run in background and return a cell_id immediately. Use wait(cell_id, yield_time_ms) to long-poll for output/exit status.

function.name: sql_query
function.description: Execute read-only SQL queries (SELECT only). Supports SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL. Connection URL format: sqlite://path.db, mysql://user:pass@host/db, postgresql://user:pass@host/db

query.description: SQL query to execute (only SELECT / SHOW / DESCRIBE / EXPLAIN allowed)

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from page.next_cursor; reuse only with identical parameters

function.name: task_create
function.description: Atomically create the complete task graph in one call. Always put every task in the tasks array, including a single task; never split one graph across concurrent task_create calls. Dependencies are optional; use base_revision when adding tasks to an existing graph.

tasks.description: The complete atomic task graph. Include every related task in this one array, even when it contains only one task. Dependency ids may refer to this batch or existing tasks.

id.description: Stable task id unique within this run

title.description: User-visible task title in the user's current language; keep technical identifiers unchanged

description.description: Subagent brief in the user's current language; keep code, paths, commands, and technical identifiers unchanged

extension.description: Product-owned task data ignored by framework scheduling

base_revision.description: Required when the current TaskRun already has tasks.

reason.description: Why these tasks are being added

function.name: task_list
function.description: List the current TaskRun's tasks, dependency-aware graph revision, and runtime status. Results are bounded; use limit, cursor, and detail_level=full to page through the same committed graph without creating another task store.

limit.description: Maximum tasks returned in one page.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor returned in the previous page metadata.

detail_level.description: Summary returns id/title/status; full also includes dependencies, retry count, and status detail.

function.name: task_update
function.description: Atomically update task specifications, dependency relations, ordering, or skip state using optimistic concurrency. Only pending or blocked task specifications may change while a run is active.

reason.description: Why runtime evidence requires this revision

id.description: Stable task id unique within this run

title.description: User-visible task title in the user's current language; keep technical identifiers unchanged

description.description: Subagent brief in the user's current language; keep code, paths, commands, and technical identifiers unchanged

extension.description: Product-owned task data ignored by framework scheduling

title.description: User-visible task title in the user's current language

description.description: Subagent brief in the user's current language

extension.description: Product-owned task data ignored by framework scheduling

function.name: text_stats
function.description: Statistics for text files: line count, word count, character count, etc.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the text file

function.name: topn_data
function.description: Sort by a metric column and take Top N. Without dimension columns, returns global top N; with dimension_columns specified, returns top N within each group. Suitable for questions like 'top 10 products by sales', 'top 3 categories by revenue in each region'. Example: topn_data(file_path='sales.csv', metric_column='revenue', dimension_columns='region', top_n=3)

file_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

dimension_columns.description: Grouping dimension columns (optional, comma-separated). Global sort if not specified

ascending.description: Whether to sort ascending (default false, i.e., descending)

function.name: transform_data
function.description: Transform data: sort, select columns, rename columns, drop columns, etc.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the data file

params.description: Operation params. sort: 'col:asc/desc'; select: 'col1,col2'; drop: 'col1,col2'; rename: 'old:new' (one pair) or 'old1:new1,old2:new2' (multiple pairs)

function.name: view_image
function.description: View a local image file when visual inspection is needed. The image pixels are sent directly to multimodal models.
